newsitem.title: UK: Biotech companies will overcome doubt, banker says.
newsitem.headline: Biotech companies will overcome doubt, banker says.

text.p: Europe's biotechnology sector may see some peaks and troughs but it represents good value to investors, a U.S. investment banker said on Wednesday.

Doubts among consumers about the safety of genetic engineering could easily be dispelled with a little education, said Dennis Purcell, managing director for life science at New York investment bankers Hambrecht and Quist.
"The biotech sector is alive and well now in Europe," he told Reuters ahead of a European Growth conference in London sponsored by the bank.
He predicted the European biotech market would see some dramatic ups and downs before investors got used to the way it worked, with dramatic new discoveries and equally dramatic failures.
"There's an element of maturity in the U.S. market that we may not see here yet," Purcell said.

He said European investors had not yet been through the roller-coaster ride that U.S. investors had. Considering that one in 10 drugs failed to reach the market, some volatility could only be expected.
"The science in Europe is as attractive if not more attractive than the U.S.," he added, saying this woud lead to "We are going to see more and more companies go public."
Industry experts say the biotechnology industry is booming across Europe, with employment up 50 percent, and 15 percent annual growth.

Purcell said he was not worried about a survey, published on Wednesday in the science journal Nature, that found the European public was overwhelmingly mistrustful of biotechnology and biotech companies.
"I think the U.S. went through the same process 10 years ago when there were a lot of questions in people's minds about what biotechnology was," he said.
"In Europe you haven't had the first stage," he added. "Now Europe is being hit with sophisticated technology."
Purcell said lobbyists had helped educate people about the issues.

"I think over time, with education, they will come to accept biotechnology," he said. Having an overall European group speaking on behalf of biotechnology, like the U.S. Biotechnology Industry Association (BIO), would help, he added.
The survey showed particular mistrust among Europeans for genetically engineering animals. Purcell said this would change as people understood that useful drugs could spring from the science.
